나.forms: subject: 내가 · object: 나를 · my: 내 (내 친구)
나.e: Casual 'I' (humble: 저); becomes 내가 before 가, and 내 = my.

편의점.x: I bought water at the convenience store.
편의점.e: 편의 (convenience) + 점 (store) — 'convenience store' word for word.
편의점.t: Pronounced [펴니점]: 의 in a non-initial syllable sounds like 이.

정류장.x: I'm waiting for my friend at the bus stop.
정류장.e: Literally 'stop-and-stay place'. 버스 정류장 = bus stop.
정류장.t: Pronounced [정뉴장]: ㄹ after ㅇ becomes ㄴ.

없다.m: to not be (somewhere), to not exist; to not have

잘.forms: 잘 + verb: 잘 먹겠습니다 · 잘 자요 · 잘하다 (to be good at)
잘.t: Many set phrases: 잘 먹겠습니다 (before eating), 잘 지내요? (how are you?).

힘.ex: 아침을 못 먹어서 힘이 하나도 없어요.
힘.x: I couldn't eat breakfast, so I have no energy at all.
힘.e: The base of 힘들다 (hard, tiring) and 힘내다 (to cheer up).
힘.t: 힘내세요! is the classic way to say 'Hang in there!' or 'You can do it!'
rel: to cheer up, to keep going

마르다.forms: 말라요 · 말랐어요 · 마를 거예요 · 마른 (+noun) (르 irregular)
마르다.m: to be thin, to be skinny; to dry, to dry up
마르다.x: My younger sibling is so thin that I'm worried.
마르다.e: One verb, two senses: water 'drying up' and a body 'thinning out'.
마르다.t: Use the past to describe someone: 말랐어요 'is thin'; and 목이 말라요 means 'I'm thirsty'.

연예인.ex: 길에서 유명한 연예인을 봐서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
연예인.x: I was surprised to see a famous celebrity on the street.
연예인.e: Literally 'performing-arts person': singers, actors, TV hosts.

키우다.m: to raise, to bring up; to keep (a pet), to grow (plants)
키우다.ex: 저는 집에서 고양이 두 마리를 키워요.
키우다.x: I have two cats at home.
키우다.e: From 크다 'to be big' + causative -이우-: literally 'make big'.

늘.x: That friend always has a smiling face.
늘.e: Don't confuse it with 늘다 (to increase) — a different word.

자세히.forms: 자세히 + verb; 자세하다 = to be detailed
자세히.x: The teacher explained the grammar in detail.
자세히.e: Literally 'careful and fine' — looking at the fine details.

제대로.forms: 제대로 + verb; often 제대로 못 + verb
제대로.m: properly, right, as it should be
제대로.x: I couldn't sleep properly last night.
제대로.e: 제 'its own' + 대로 'according to' — 'in its proper way'.

직접.forms: 직접 + verb: 직접 만들다, 직접 가다
직접.e: Literally 'direct contact' — no one in between.
직접.t: Pronounced [직쩝] — the ㅈ tenses after the ㄱ batchim.

피부과.x: My skin was so itchy that I went to the dermatologist.

식욕.x: I have no appetite these days because of stress.
식욕.t: 식욕 is a bit formal; in daily talk people say 입맛이 없어요.

어린 시절.x: I lived in the countryside as a child.
어린 시절.e: 어린 (young, from 어리다) + 시절 (period of life).

배우자.ex: 이 서류에 배우자 이름도 써 주세요.
배우자.x: Please also write your spouse's name on this form.
배우자.e: Literally 'the person paired with you'; a formal word for husband or wife.
배우자.t: Watch out: 배우자! can also mean 'Let's learn!' (배우다 + -자).

고마워하다.x: My friend really appreciated my help.
고마워하다.e: From 고맙다 'thankful' plus -어하다, describing someone else's gratitude.

롤러코스터.x: The roller coaster was so scary that I screamed.
롤러코스터.t: Older people may call it 청룡열차 'blue dragon train', after one of Korea's first coasters.

딩동.e: 의성어 (sound word) imitating a two-tone doorbell or chime.
딩동.t: 딩동댕 is the chime for a correct answer on quiz shows; a wrong answer gets 땡.

캠페인.ex: 학교에서 쓰레기 줄이기 캠페인을 하고 있어요.
캠페인.x: The school is running a campaign to reduce trash.
캠페인.e: From English 'campaign'; mostly for public-awareness drives, while election campaigns are usually 선거 운동.

미디어.x: We need education on using the media wisely.

리포트.x: I have to turn in my paper by Friday.
리포트.e: From English 'report'; at Korean colleges it means a term paper or written assignment.

연구실.x: The professor is in his office right now.
연구실.t: A professor's office is also called 연구실, not 사무실.

메모리.x: There isn't enough memory, so the app keeps shutting down.
메모리.e: From English 'memory'; only the computer sense, a person's memory is 기억.

방사능.ex: 사고 후에 그 지역의 방사능 수치가 높아졌어요.
방사능.x: After the accident, radiation levels in the area went up.
방사능.t: 방사능 is radioactivity; the rays themselves are 방사선, as in an X-ray.

대단히.x: Thank you very much for your help.
대단히.t: 대단히 감사합니다 and 대단히 죄송합니다 are standard formal phrases.

유모차.x: I put the baby in the stroller and took a walk in the park.
유모차.t: 'Push a stroller' is 유모차를 밀다; 'put a baby in' is 태우다, the same verb as giving someone a ride.

확충하다.m: to expand, to enlarge and reinforce (facilities, resources)
확충하다.ex: 시는 어린이집 등 보육 시설을 확충할 계획입니다.
확충하다.x: The city plans to expand childcare facilities such as daycare centers.

탐욕스럽다.ex: 탐욕스러운 사람은 아무리 가져도 만족하지 못해요.
탐욕스럽다.x: A greedy person is never satisfied, no matter how much they have.

일거양득.m: killing two birds with one stone, a double benefit
일거양득.x: I get exercise and save money, so it's two birds with one stone.

돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라.forms: 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라는 말처럼 · 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너야죠
돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라.m: look before you leap; be careful even when something seems safe
돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라.ex: 돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라는 말처럼 계약서는 꼼꼼히 읽어야 해요.
돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라.x: As they say, look before you leap, so read the contract carefully.
돌다리도 두들겨 보고 건너라.e: Literally 'tap even a stone bridge before you cross it.'
nb: 개구리 올챙이 적 생각 못 한다

혀를 내두르다.ex: 그 아이의 피아노 실력에 모두가 혀를 내둘렀어요.
혀를 내두르다.x: Everyone was amazed by the child's piano skills.
혀를 내두르다.e: Literally 'to swing one's tongue around' — left speechless in amazement.
혀를 내두르다.t: Don't confuse with 혀를 차다 'to click one's tongue in disapproval.'

제조사.ex: 휴대폰이 고장 나서 제조사에 수리를 맡겼어요.
제조사.x: My phone broke, so I sent it to the manufacturer for repair.
제조사.t: 제조사 makes physical goods; 제작사 is used for films, TV shows and games.

개인전.ex: 그 화가는 다음 달에 첫 개인전을 열어요.
개인전.x: That painter is holding her first solo exhibition next month.
개인전.t: The usual verb is 열다: 개인전을 열다, 'to hold a solo show'.

변함없이.ex: 할아버지는 변함없이 매일 아침 산책을 하세요.
변함없이.x: As always, my grandfather takes a walk every morning.

기리다.m: to honor, to commemorate, to pay tribute to
기리다.ex: 우리는 매년 그분의 업적을 기리는 행사를 엽니다.
기리다.x: Every year we hold an event to honor his achievements.
기리다.t: Typical objects: 업적 (achievements), 뜻 (wishes), 넋 (spirit), 희생 (sacrifice), usually of people who have passed.

사문화.m: becoming a dead letter, falling into disuse (of a law)
사문화.x: That law effectively became a dead letter long ago.
사문화.e: Literally 'becoming dead writing': a law that exists on paper but is never enforced.
사문화.t: Mostly used as 사문화되다; it is the exact counterpart of the English idiom 'dead letter'.

인허가.ex: 공장을 지으려면 여러 가지 인허가 절차를 거쳐야 해요.
인허가.x: To build a factory, you have to go through various permit procedures.
인허가.e: A blend of 인가 (authorization) and 허가 (permission).
인허가.t: Usually combined: 인허가 절차 (permit process), 인허가를 받다 (obtain permits).

피란민.ex: 전쟁 중에 수많은 피란민이 부산으로 몰려들었어요.
피란민.x: During the war, countless refugees flooded into Busan.
피란민.t: 피란 means fleeing war; 피난 means fleeing any disaster, and people often mix them up.

백골난망.m: eternal gratitude, a kindness never forgotten even after death
백골난망.ex: 어려울 때 도와주신 은혜는 정말 백골난망입니다.
백골난망.x: I will never forget how you helped me in hard times, even after I die.
백골난망.e: Literally 'hard to forget even as white bones' — gratitude that outlasts death.
백골난망.t: Very formal and old-fashioned; used to thank someone deeply for a great favor.

황망하다.m: flustered, in a frantic hurry; sudden and shocking (news of a death)
황망하다.ex: 친구 아버님의 황망한 부고를 듣고 말을 잃었어요.
황망하다.x: I was speechless when I heard the sudden news of my friend's father's passing.
황망하다.e: Literally 'hurried and busy': so rushed you lose your composure.
황망하다.t: Common in condolences: 황망한 소식, 황망한 마음 for a sudden, shocking loss.
rel: to have no time to think

병리현상.ex: 청소년 자살은 우리 사회의 심각한 병리현상입니다.
병리현상.x: Youth suicide is a serious pathology of our society.
병리현상.t: Pronounced [병니현상]: ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.
